raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm not a young farmer anymore — 63 years old, just me and my husband at home now, and he helps some but can't do what he used to. The kids send a little money but they work in town. So labor is tight, and I can't spend money I don't have.

My 4.1 mu is split — about 3 mu I keep in the wheat-maize rotation like most folks around here, and the other 1.1 mu is a little cotton patch on the sandier ground near the road. Cotton has been rough the last few years, prices aren't great and the picking is hard on my back, but I'm used to growing it and that piece of land doesn't do as well for grain.

**For the wheat** (already in the ground since last October): I put down about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's my base. Now in spring, when it's jointing, I'll topdress urea, maybe 20-25 jin per mu. Total nitrogen works out to around 16 kg/mu, which is what the village extension fellow says is about right, and it matches what I've been doing. I irrigate the winter water in late November if it's dry, then again at jointing, and one more time at grain filling if the rain doesn't come. Three waterings usually. Last year I got about 420 kg/mu — hoping for similar. I'll hire the combine at harvest, everyone does.

**For the maize**, I go straight in after wheat — no time to plow properly, I just use the no-till planter that the cooperative rents out. Zhengdan 958 seed, the variety my neighbor's been getting good yields with. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage. About 15 kg N/mu total. If it's a dry July I'll irrigate once. My husband and I can manage the harvest by hand on 3 mu, though my back isn't what it was — might hire a half-day of help.

**For the cotton**: I plant mid-to-late April on that 1.1 mu. I use saved seed mixed with some new — cotton is expensive if you buy all new every year. Base fertilizer before planting, about 12 kg N/mu total for the season. Cotton needs more pesticide than the other crops — bollworm, aphids — so I budget maybe 80 yuan/mu for sprays. The picking is the problem. I'll do what I can and pay a neighbor to help for a few days in the picking season. Honestly, if cotton prices don't pick up, next year I might plant it all to peanut or something.

I keep a little cash aside — maybe 500 yuan — because something always comes up. Pump breaks, or the price of urea jumps. You learn after 40 years not to spend everything at planting time.
